explanations: onSellerProfileChanged uses updateOne with the filter {"seller.id": sellerId}. A seller typically has many listings, but updateOne modifies only the first matching document. All other listings keep the old displayName and rating in search results until each is individually re-indexed. It should be updateMany.

Embedding read-time data is the classic denormalization tradeoff: search() projects seller.displayName and seller.rating directly, avoiding N extra lookups, but changes to a seller must be fanned out. ObjectId references are fine in subdocuments, embedding doesn't affect the keywords index size, and search() doesn't filter on rating.

tokenize lowercases and splits both titles and queries, and the filter uses keywords: {$all: terms}, requiring every term. $all is not OR, there's no exact-title match, and lowercasing on both sides removes case sensitivity.

indexListing uses replaceOne({_id}, doc, {upsert: true}), which is idempotent per _id: the second call replaces the document with the same content. No duplicate is created, upsert on _id doesn't raise duplicate key errors here, and indexedAt is never checked.
